cards.name: Poster Edges
cards.summary: Photoshop Effect (Filter Gallery) that posterizes the rasterized artwork to a few flat tones and draws dark black lines along its contrast edges, giving a printed-poster / comic look. On flat vector art the main visible change is dark, slightly ragged black outlines (thick only at a high Edge Thickness) around every shape plus banding in gradients.
use_for: comic or pop-art outline treatment on a flat illustration
gritty gig-poster or zine look on placed artwork
stylising a placed photo inside an Illustrator layout to match a cartoon set
banding a gradient into flat poster tones with inked edges
avoid: Greyed out in CMYK documents: the Filter Gallery effects need an RGB document (File > Document Color Mode > RGB) or do the look in Photoshop.
Clean vector outlines: the edges are raster and pixel-sized; for crisp scalable outlines use a stroke, Effect > Path > Offset Path or Outline Stroke instead.
Small type: the black edge lines fill in counters and kill legibility.
Scripted pipelines that need chosen values: applyEffect cannot send the effect's settings (render check of the scripted apply barely changed the probe, mean diff 0.51).

params.name: Edge Thickness
params.does: width of the black lines drawn along contrast edges
params.typical: 2 for a fine ink line, 6-8 for heavy comic outlines

params.name: Edge Intensity
params.does: how dark the edge lines are and how many lower-contrast edges also get lines
params.typical: 1-2 subtle, 4-6 strong inked look

params.name: Posterization
params.does: sets how many tone levels the colours are reduced to (the posterize step); shows as banding in gradients and photos, little change on flat fills
params.typical: 2 (dialog value at harvest) for clear poster banding

pairs_with: Effect > Artistic > Cutout for flatter colour shapes under the outlines
Effect > Texture > Grain for a printed-paper finish
Document Raster Effects Settings (raise to 300 ppi for print before judging line weight)
cards.scripting: item.applyEffect('<LiveEffect name="PSAdapter_plugin_PstE"><Dict data="I dataSize 68 I PrevDres 300 B go 1"/></LiveEffect>') applies the live effect, but Edge Thickness / Edge Intensity / Posterization live in the binary 'data' descriptor that Dict data cannot carry, so the result uses whatever settings the plug-in falls back to. For chosen values: select the item and app.executeMenuCommand('Live PSAdapter_plugin_PstE'), which opens the 'Poster Edges (100%)' dialog with the last-used values and needs OK; or build the look once by hand, save it as a Graphic Style and apply it with doc.graphicStyles.getByName('<style>').applyTo(item). Gallery route (2026-10-13): a plain applyEffect cannot carry the dialog settings (the Photoshop parameter block is binary 'data' that Dict data cannot send); the gallery applies the effect, saves the file, writes the dialog's parameter dictionary into it and reopens it, and that route renders the chosen values pixel-identical to the dialog (Dark Strokes control).
cards.non_destructive: yes: a live effect in the Appearance panel (double-click to edit); Object > Expand Appearance bakes it into an embedded image
cards.cost: medium: rasterizes the object at the Document Raster Effects resolution (PrevDres 300 recorded) through the Filter Gallery; slows redraw on large artwork

review.changes: Posterization 'does' no longer claims a direction (higher = stronger reduction was unsupported by the harvest, which has no range); summary no longer calls the outlines thick at the harvested Edge Thickness 2.

verified.note: At Edge Thickness 10 / Intensity 10 (the re-rendered demo) the photo is posterized to a few flat tones with dark ragged ink lines along every contrast edge and the grey ramp broken into steps, the printed-poster / comic look the card describes; demo_settings restored to the values the frame was rendered with.

cards.name: Rough Pastels
cards.summary: Photoshop Effect (Filter Gallery) that redraws the artwork as coloured pastel-chalk strokes over an embossed texture (canvas by default): bright areas get thick chalk with little texture, darker areas look scraped so the texture shows through. Flat vector fills turn into streaky chalk on a lit, bumpy surface.
use_for: hand-drawn chalk or pastel look for a poster illustration
textured, crafty treatment of flat icons or badges
children's book or menu artwork that should feel drawn rather than vector
adding paper / canvas tooth to a flat colour block
avoid: Greyed out in CMYK documents: the Filter Gallery effects need an RGB document.
Text and fine line art: chalk strokes break up thin strokes and small type.
When only a surface texture is wanted without streaks: use Effect > Texture > Texturizer instead.
Scripted pipelines that need chosen values: applyEffect cannot send stroke, texture or light settings.

params.name: Stroke Length
params.does: length of the chalk strokes; longer gives streakier, more directional marks
params.typical: 6 (dialog value at harvest) subtle, 20-30 bold streaks

params.name: Stroke Detail
params.does: how sharply the chalk strokes are imprinted; higher gives crisper, more visible marks

params.name: Texture Type
params.does: surface texture under the chalk (the dialog offers several, e.g. canvas, brick, burlap, sandstone); the harvest recorded only the default code TxCa
params.typical: TxCa (default)

params.name: Scaling
params.does: size of the texture pattern in percent
params.typical: 100 default, 150-180 for a coarse visible weave

params.name: Relief
params.does: depth of the embossed texture
params.typical: 20 default, 30-40 strongly embossed

params.name: Light Direction
params.does: side the texture is lit from, which sets where the emboss highlights fall
params.typical: Top Left or Bottom

params.name: Invert Texture
params.does: swaps texture peaks and valleys
params.typical: false

pairs_with: Effect > Distort & Transform > Roughen for wobbly hand-drawn edges before the chalk
Effect > Texture > Grain for extra paper speckle
Document Raster Effects Settings (stroke size is in pixels, so the look gets finer at higher ppi)
cards.scripting: item.applyEffect('<LiveEffect name="PSAdapter_plugin_RghP"><Dict data="I dataSize 129 I PrevDres 300 B go 1"/></LiveEffect>') applies the live effect, but every chalk / texture / light setting lives in the binary 'data' descriptor that Dict data cannot carry, so the scripted result uses the plug-in's fallback settings. For chosen values: select the item and app.executeMenuCommand('Live PSAdapter_plugin_RghP') (opens the 'Rough Pastels (100%)' dialog with last-used values, needs OK), or save a hand-made version as a Graphic Style and doc.graphicStyles.getByName('<style>').applyTo(item). Gallery route (2026-10-13): a plain applyEffect cannot carry the dialog settings (the Photoshop parameter block is binary 'data' that Dict data cannot send); the gallery applies the effect, saves the file, writes the dialog's parameter dictionary into it and reopens it, and that route renders the chosen values pixel-identical to the dialog (Dark Strokes control).
cards.non_destructive: yes: a live effect in the Appearance panel; Object > Expand Appearance bakes it into an embedded image
cards.cost: medium-high: Filter Gallery stroke plus texture pass at the Document Raster Effects resolution (PrevDres 300 recorded); noticeably slow on large objects

review.changes: Stroke Detail 'does' reworded (the claim that it keeps more of the artwork's edge detail was unsupported).

verified.note: The photo is redrawn as streaky diagonal pastel-chalk strokes over a bumpy, lit canvas texture, the strip blocks streaked at their edges and the type broken up, as the card describes.

cards.name: Smudge Stick
cards.summary: Photoshop Effect (Filter Gallery) that softens the artwork with short diagonal strokes that smear the darker areas, while lighter areas get brighter and lose detail. Flat vector shapes get smudged, diagonally streaked edges and a slightly blown-out, chalky-bright interior.
use_for: soft smudged-crayon or charcoal-smear look on illustration
knocking crisp vector edges back into a painterly, rubbed texture
dreamy, washed background artwork behind sharp headline type
avoid: Greyed out in CMYK documents: the Filter Gallery effects need an RGB document.
Type and logos that must stay readable: the diagonal smear and highlight wash eat thin strokes.
When the aim is just softness: Effect > Blur > Gaussian Blur gives a clean blur without streaks or brightening.
Scripted pipelines that need chosen values: applyEffect cannot send the stroke settings.

flat vector fills: on flat or very smooth art this filter has nothing to stroke and only remaps brightness, so at these values every colour without a channel at 255 (gradients, dark greys, a flat red) is only scaled darker (the test plate's gradient to about x0.82, with no strokes) while fills with a full channel (pure orange, pure blue) survive; that is Illustrator's own result (a dialog-applied control matched the scripted render pixel for pixel), so give it a photo or textured art

params.name: Stroke Length
params.does: length of the diagonal smudge strokes
params.typical: 2 (dialog value at harvest) subtle, 6-8 clearly streaked

params.name: Highlight Area
params.does: how much of the lighter range is pushed brighter and flattened
params.typical: 0 (dialog value at harvest) none, 8-12 bright washed highlights

params.name: Intensity
params.does: strength of the highlight brightening
params.typical: 10 (dialog value at harvest) for strong brightening, 4-8 gentler

pairs_with: Effect > Texture > Grain or Texturizer to add paper tooth under the smear
Effect > Brush Strokes > Dark Strokes for a darker, moodier variant
Document Raster Effects Settings (stroke length is in pixels)
cards.scripting: item.applyEffect('<LiveEffect name="PSAdapter_plugin_SmdS"><Dict data="I dataSize 84 I PrevDres 300 B go 1"/></LiveEffect>') applies the live effect, but Stroke Length / Highlight Area / Intensity live in the binary 'data' descriptor that Dict data cannot carry, so the scripted result uses fallback settings (the harvest probe darkened slightly, mean diff 2.47). For chosen values: select the item and app.executeMenuCommand('Live PSAdapter_plugin_SmdS') (opens the 'Smudge Stick (100%)' dialog with last-used values, needs OK), or apply a hand-made Graphic Style with doc.graphicStyles.getByName('<style>').applyTo(item). The stored random seed differs on every application, so two applies never match pixel for pixel. Gallery route (2026-10-13): a plain applyEffect cannot carry the dialog settings (the Photoshop parameter block is binary 'data' that Dict data cannot send); the gallery applies the effect, saves the file, writes the dialog's parameter dictionary into it and reopens it, and that route renders the chosen values pixel-identical to the dialog (Dark Strokes control).
cards.non_destructive: yes: a live effect in the Appearance panel; Object > Expand Appearance bakes it into an embedded image
cards.cost: medium: one Filter Gallery pass at the Document Raster Effects resolution (PrevDres 300 recorded)

review.changes: demo Intensity 7 -> 10 (the harvested dialog value, so it is in range and makes the highlight wash obvious on a flat vector fill); Intensity typical now cites the harvested 10.

verified.note: At Stroke Length 10 / Highlight Area 20 / Intensity 10 (the re-rendered demo) the darker areas are smeared with short diagonal strokes and the light areas brighten into a washed, blown-out yellow, losing detail, the smudge-stick look the card describes; demo_settings restored to the values the frame was rendered with.

cards.name: Sponge
cards.summary: Photoshop Effect (Filter Gallery) that simulates sponge painting: the artwork breaks into highly textured, mottled patches of contrasting colour. Flat fills become blotchy, porous dabs and edges go soft and irregular.
use_for: sponge-painted or stamped texture inside flat colour shapes
rustic, faux-finish treatment for posters, labels and packaging art
breaking up large flat areas so they feel hand-made
avoid: Greyed out in CMYK documents: the Filter Gallery effects need an RGB document.
Small type and thin lines: the mottling dissolves them.
When an even film-grain speckle is wanted rather than blotches: use Effect > Texture > Grain or Effect > Artistic > Film Grain.
Scripted pipelines that need chosen values: applyEffect cannot send the brush settings.

params.name: Brush Size
params.does: size of the sponge dabs
params.typical: 2 (dialog value at harvest) fine, 7-9 big blotches

params.name: Definition
params.does: contrast and crispness of the dab pattern; higher gives harder, darker mottling
params.typical: 12 (dialog value at harvest), 18-22 strong

params.name: Smoothness
params.does: softens the dab edges; low values look rougher
params.typical: 1-3 rough, 5 (dialog value at harvest) softer

pairs_with: Effect > Artistic > Cutout first to flatten colour, then Sponge for the texture
Opacity / blend mode in the Appearance panel to tone the mottling down
Document Raster Effects Settings (dab size is in pixels)

For chosen values: select the item and app.executeMenuCommand('Live PSAdapter_plugin_Spng') (opens the 'Sponge (100%)' dialog with last-used values, needs OK), or apply a hand-made Graphic Style with doc.graphicStyles.getByName('<style>').applyTo(item). The stored random seed differs on every application. Gallery route (2026-10-13): a plain applyEffect cannot carry the dialog settings (the Photoshop parameter block is binary 'data' that Dict data cannot send); the gallery applies the effect, saves the file, writes the dialog's parameter dictionary into it and reopens it, and that route renders the chosen values pixel-identical to the dialog (Dark Strokes control).
cards.non_destructive: yes: a live effect in the Appearance panel; Object > Expand Appearance bakes it into an embedded image
cards.cost: medium: one Filter Gallery pass at the Document Raster Effects resolution (PrevDres 300 recorded)

verified.note: The whole photo, strip and ramp break into porous, mottled sponge patches of contrasting tone, the sponge-painted look the card describes.

cards.name: Underpainting
cards.summary: Photoshop Effect (Filter Gallery) that paints the artwork onto a textured background and then paints the image again over it, giving a soft, blurred, slightly muted painting on embossed canvas. Vector shapes lose their crisp edges to broad brushwork with visible canvas texture.
use_for: soft painted-on-canvas look for a poster or book-cover illustration
turning flat vector art into a fine-art print feel
muted textured background art behind sharp type
avoid: Greyed out in CMYK documents: the Filter Gallery effects need an RGB document.
Anything that must stay sharp (logos, small type): the brushwork blurs edges heavily at large Brush Size.
When only canvas texture is needed without the blur: Effect > Texture > Texturizer.
Scripted pipelines that need chosen values: applyEffect cannot send brush, texture or light settings.

params.name: Brush Size
params.does: size of the underpainting brush; larger blurs shapes more
params.typical: 6 (dialog value at harvest) light, 20-30 broad and soft

params.name: Texture Coverage
params.does: how much of the image the textured underpainting covers
params.typical: 16 (dialog value at harvest), 25-35 heavy texture

params.name: Texture Type
params.does: surface texture (the dialog offers several, e.g. canvas, brick, burlap, sandstone); the harvest recorded only the default code TxCa
params.typical: TxCa (default)

params.name: Scaling
params.does: size of the texture pattern in percent
params.typical: 100 default, 150-180 coarse

params.name: Relief
params.does: depth of the embossed texture
params.typical: 4 (dialog value at harvest) faint, 15-25 clearly embossed

params.name: Light Direction
params.does: side the texture is lit from
params.typical: Top (dialog value at harvest) or Top Left

params.name: Invert Texture
params.does: swaps texture peaks and valleys
params.typical: false

pairs_with: Effect > Artistic > Dry Brush or Paint Daubs stacked above for more defined strokes
Effect > Texture > Texturizer for a stronger single texture
Document Raster Effects Settings (brush size is in pixels)

cards.name: Watercolor
cards.summary: Photoshop Effect (Filter Gallery) that repaints the artwork in a watercolour style with a medium wet brush that simplifies detail and saturates colour where strong tonal edges occur. The result is blotchy, saturated and noticeably darker, with dark pooled edges; it is a stylised filter look, not a light transparent wash.
use_for: quick painted, blotchy colour treatment on illustration or placed photos
saturated, inky watercolour-style poster art
stylising flat icons so they read as painted
avoid: Greyed out in CMYK documents: the Filter Gallery effects need an RGB document.
Wanting a light, airy wash: this filter darkens and muddies; keep Shadow Intensity low or use transparent fills with Effect > Stylize > Feather instead.
Small type: the brush simplification swallows it.

flat vector fills: on flat or very smooth art this filter has nothing to stroke and only remaps brightness, so at these values every colour without a channel at 255 (gradients, dark greys, a flat red) goes near-solid black while fills with a full channel (pure orange, pure blue) survive; that is Illustrator's own result (a dialog-applied control matched the scripted render pixel for pixel), so give it a photo or textured art

params.name: Brush Detail
params.does: how much detail the brush keeps; low values give big simplified blobs
params.typical: 9 (dialog value at harvest), 3-6 for a looser painted look

params.name: Shadow Intensity
params.does: how strongly dark areas are deepened; high values go nearly black
params.typical: 1 (dialog value at harvest); keep 0-3, higher goes muddy

params.name: Texture
params.does: amount of paper-like texture in the paint
params.typical: 1 (dialog value at harvest) smooth, 3 clearly textured

pairs_with: Effect > Texture > Texturizer for a paper surface
Appearance panel Opacity / Multiply over a light paper fill to soften the darkening
Document Raster Effects Settings (brush is pixel-sized)
cards.scripting: item.applyEffect('<LiveEffect name="PSAdapter_plugin_Wtrc"><Dict data="I dataSize 68 I PrevDres 300 B go 1"/></LiveEffect>') applies the live effect, but Brush Detail / Shadow Intensity / Texture live in the binary 'data' descriptor that Dict data cannot carry; the harvest's scripted render of a flat red came out solid black, which is this filter's brightness remap on flat fills (a dialog-applied control gives the same), not a route fault. For chosen values: select the item and app.executeMenuCommand('Live PSAdapter_plugin_Wtrc') (opens the 'Watercolor (100%)' dialog with last-used values, needs OK), or apply a hand-made Graphic Style with doc.graphicStyles.getByName('<style>').applyTo(item). Gallery route (2026-10-13): a plain applyEffect cannot carry the dialog settings (the Photoshop parameter block is binary 'data' that Dict data cannot send); the gallery applies the effect, saves the file, writes the dialog's parameter dictionary into it and reopens it, and that route renders the chosen values pixel-identical to the dialog (Dark Strokes control).
cards.non_destructive: yes: a live effect in the Appearance panel; Object > Expand Appearance bakes it into an embedded image
cards.cost: medium: one Filter Gallery pass at the Document Raster Effects resolution (PrevDres 300 recorded)

review.changes: Texture typical no longer states 3 as the maximum (no range in the harvest); Shadow Intensity typical now cites the harvested 1.

verified.note: On the photo detail is simplified into blotchy, saturated and noticeably darker patches with dark pooled edges (the dark areas go near-black, the strip stays saturated), the watercolour filter look the card describes; the old black gradient on the vector plate was its brightness remap on flat fills, now a card fact, not a route fault.
